text:
Asha: heads-up — new model nightingale-q4 landed in canary and parse errors for funcall JSON jumped (~3x) vs baseline. sample below from failed batch where tool payload got cut mid-stream.
Pieter: ugh, same as when batching crosses chunk boundaries. are we running continuous-batching for this canary? :thinking:
Asha: yes, continuous-batching enabled to mirror prod. repro snippet from the canary logs: 
```
INVOKE id=abc123 model=nightingale-q4 mode=batch-slice
OUT >> {\"tool\":\"search\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"how to bake scone\",\"k\":5}\n...<stream cut>...\nINVOKE failed: json.DecodeError: unexpected EOF
```
Sam: can you paste request/response headers? curious about transfer-encoding: chunked interactions.
Asha: headers look normal. It only happens when request size > ~1.6k tokens and the batch slice splits inside the JSON. smaller batches are fine. sometimes model appends a trailing \n sentinel and it parses.
Melanie: two coexisting behaviours: (1) the model emits complete JSON + newline sentinel, (2) it stops mid-JSON when the slice boundary cuts a toolcall. could be cutoff policy + batch scheduling race.
Pieter: hypothesis: int4 quant changed tokenization/packing slightly, shifting slice boundaries. the batch-slice cut point is deterministic but small tokenization variance moves a comma/brace into next slice => truncated JSON.
Sam: quick mitigations we can try:
- increase slice margin so we avoid cutting inside likely tool outputs
- append an explicit sentinel suffix to toolcall prompts (e.g. "__END_TOOL__") and accept at parse time
- fallback json-repair heuristics on parse failure (temporary)
Asha: can we run a micro-canary with sentinel suffix enabled? perf hit ok for an hour to validate.
eval-bot: Canary summary (nightingale-q4): parse error rate baseline 0.7% -> canary 2.8% over 2k calls. top error: unexpected EOF during parse (72%). dashboard: https://redwood.internal/canary/1719876543
Melanie: quick patch plan:
1) ship sentinel-suffix toggle to canary (runtime flag)
2) micro-canary 1h with same traffic but reduce continuous-batch size 64->32
3) collect EOF examples and run offline json-repair to quantify auto-heal rate
4) if sentinel fixes >80% of failures, move to dedicated canaries and then tweak batch cutter to avoid cutting inside top-level { or [ when possible
Pieter: I'll prototype a preflight lint on the first streaming chunk to cheaply detect likely mid-JSON slices (heuristics: unbalanced braces, trailing comma, unfinished string). cheap and fast, can reject early or trigger a small re-request.
Sam: also add telemetry tag for "sentinel-accepted" vs "repair-applied" so we can measure how many responses relied on heuristics.
Asha: timeline? can we have sentinel toggle in canary by EOD?
Melanie: I'll open a tiny runtime flag PR now, set to off by default, will enable in our canary config once merged. aim to run micro-canary tomorrow morning and report.
Pieter: sending a quick script to gather 100 EOF examples from the last 24h and push to /tmp/canary-eofs.tar.gz. will attach to the triage ticket.
Asha: thanks — let's keep this thread for updates and paste a few raw failed payloads here as we collect them.
